mainTopic: Who has a share in עולם הבא: the דור המדבר, the עשרת השבטים, and young children
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of קרח's group, who admit from inside גיהנם that משה and his תורה are true. Next comes the משנה's line that the דור המדבר has no share in עולם הבא. A ברייתא shows this is רבי עקיבא's view. רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא say they do have a share, and רבי יהושע בן קרחה reads רבי אליעזר's proof פסוק as being about later righteous people. A new משנה argues over whether the עשרת השבטים will return, and a ברייתא extends the argument to whether they have a share in עולם הבא. Both times רבי יוחנן says רבי עקיבא 'left his kindness.' The גמרא then shows that kindness: רבי עקיבא holds that young children of wicked Jews do come to עולם הבא, against רבן גמליאל. The amud ends with several views on the age from which a child has a share: from conception, from birth, from מילה, from when he speaks, or from when he says אמן.

steps.title: The Arab tells what קרח's group cries out every thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The Arab guide explains that every thirty days גיהנם turns קרח's group around like meat in a pot, and they admit that משה and his תורה are true.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Every thirty days גיהנם turns them around like meat in a pot, and they say: 'משה and his תורה are true, and they (we) are liars.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story about the place where the ground swallowed קרח and his followers. The Arab explains the voices that can be heard there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרח's group fought against משה's leadership. Now, from inside their punishment, they keep admitting that משה was right and that they were lying. This ends the discussion of קרח's group before the גמרא moves on to the next case in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the wicked are punished after death
Liars, people who make things up

steps.whatToRemember: Even inside their punishment, קרח's group admits: 'משה and his תורה are true, and we are liars.'

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is the Arab guide talking to רבה בר בר חנה.

phrases.english: Every thirty days
גיהנם turns them back around
like meat inside a cooking pot,
and they say this:
"Moshe and his Torah are true,
and they are liars."
phrases.notes: They mean themselves. Saying 'they' instead of 'we' spares them from saying something so bad about themselves directly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה: כל תלתין יומין מהדרא להו גיהנם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story of רבה בר בר חנה and the Arab, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרח's group is punished continually, and they admit that משה and his תורה are true.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the generation of the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the דור המדבר has no share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The generation of the wilderness has no share in the World to Come, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that follows, which explains and debates it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states this as a flat rule. The ברייתא that comes next will show that this is really רבי עקיבא's view, and that other תנאים disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: The generation that left מצרים and died in the wilderness

phrases.english: The generation of the wilderness

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: have no share in the World to Come, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: דור המדבר אין להם חלק לעולם הבא וכו׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from קרח's group to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The דור המדבר has no share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא proves from two verses that they have no share
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the דור המדבר has no share in עולם הבא. רבי עקיבא proves this from 'they will be finished... and there they will die' and from the oath 'they will not come to My rest'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The generation of the wilderness has no share in the World to Come, as it says: 'In this wilderness they will be finished, and there they will die.' 'They will be finished' means in this world. 'And there they will die' means in the World to Come. And it says: 'That I swore in My anger that they would not come to My rest.' These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the source for the משנה's rule, and it tells us this is רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא sees two separate endings in one פסוק. 'Finished' is death in this world, and 'die' is losing עולם הבא. His second פסוק is an oath by ה׳ that they will never reach His 'rest', which he reads as the eternal rest of עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: They will be finished, used up

steps.confusionAlert: In a פסוק of an oath, 'אם' does not mean 'if'. It means 'not': 'I swore that they would NOT come to My rest.'

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The generation of the wilderness has no
share in the World to Come,
as it says:
"In this wilderness they will be finished,
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:35

phrases.english: and there they will die."
"They will be finished" — in this world,
"and there they will die" — in the World to Come.
And it says:
"That I swore in My anger
phrases.notes: תהלים 95:11

phrases.english: that they would not come to My rest."
phrases.notes: In an oath, 'אם' means 'not', even though it usually means 'if'.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן: דור המדבר אין להם חלק לעולם הבא, שנאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה's rule and names רבי עקיבא as its author.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the דור המדבר has no share in עולם הבא, based on במדבר 14:35 and תהלים 95:11.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר says they do come to עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees and says the דור המדבר does come to עולם הבא, based on 'Gather to Me My pious ones, who made My covenant over a sacrifice.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: They do come to the World to Come, as it says: 'Gather to Me My pious ones, who made My covenant over a sacrifice.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא in the same ברייתא takes the opposite view and brings his own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק about people who 'made a covenant over a sacrifice' as describing the דור המדבר, who made a covenant with ה׳ at הר סיני. ה׳ calls them 'My pious ones' and gathers them to Himself, so they must have a share in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
They do come to the World to Come,
as it says:
"Gather to Me My pious ones,
phrases.notes: תהלים 50:5

phrases.english: who made My covenant over a sacrifice."

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אליעזר אומר: הן באין לעולם הבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי עקיבא's conclusion and brings a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the דור המדבר does have a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר explains the oath: sworn in anger, then taken back
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר deals with רבי עקיבא's oath פסוק. ה׳ swore in anger, and then He took the oath back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do I explain 'That I swore in My anger'? In My anger I swore, and I take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר has to explain רבי עקיבא's strong פסוק, the oath that they will not come to ה׳'s rest. He reads the words 'in My anger' as a hint that the oath did not last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath seems to prove רבי עקיבא right. רבי אליעזר focuses on the word 'באפי': the oath was made only in a moment of anger, and once the anger passed, ה׳ took it back. So the פסוק does not stop them from reaching עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain (this other פסוק)?
I take it back, I change My mind

phrases.english: But how do I explain
"That I swore in My anger"?
In My anger I swore,
and I take it back.
phrases.notes: Literally 'I return in Myself': once the anger passed, ה׳ took back the oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא מה אני מקיים אשר נשבעתי באפי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem that רבי עקיבא's oath פסוק creates for רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oath in תהלים 95:11 permanently shuts the דור המדבר out of עולם הבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath was made in anger, and ה׳ later took it back, so it does not stop them.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן קרחה: 'Gather My pious ones' is about later generations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says the פסוק 'אספו לי חסידי' is about later generations, not the דור המדבר. 'My pious ones' means the righteous of every generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: This פסוק was said only about the later generations. 'Gather to Me My pious ones' means the righteous people of every generation.
steps.whatsHappening: A third תנא takes away רבי אליעזר's proof. He says the פסוק is not talking about the דור המדבר at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's whole proof rested on reading 'אספו לי חסידי' as being about the דור המדבר. If it is about righteous people of later times, it can no longer show that the דור המדבר has a share in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Later generations, the ones that come afterward

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
This verse was not said
except about the later generations.
phrases.notes: He means 'אספו לי חסידי', רבי אליעזר's פסוק. It is not about the דור המדבר.

phrases.english: "Gather to Me My pious ones" —
these are the righteous people in every single generation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהושע בן קרחה אומר: לא נאמר פסוק זה אלא כנגד דורות הבאים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-reads רבי אליעזר's פסוק so that it no longer supports his view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אליעזר's proof from 'אספו לי חסידי'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק is about righteous people of later generations, not the דור המדבר.

steps.title: The covenant-makers are those who gave up their lives for ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה continues explaining the פסוק. 'Who made My covenant' means חנניה, מישאל and עזריה in the furnace. 'Over a sacrifice' means רבי עקיבא and his colleagues, who were killed for תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who made My covenant over a sacrifice' means חנניה, מישאל and עזריה, who gave themselves over to the fiery furnace. 'Over a sacrifice' means רבי עקיבא and his colleagues, who gave themselves over to slaughter for the words of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן קרחה goes through the rest of the פסוק and shows who each phrase describes. Every phrase points to people of later generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'covenant over a sacrifice' as people who offered up their own lives, almost like a קרבן, to stay loyal to ה׳. This finishes his reading: the whole פסוק describes later martyrs and righteous people, not the people who left מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: Gave themselves over (were ready to die for ה׳)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views. רבי עקיבא: the דור המדבר has no share. רבי אליעזר: they have a share, and ה׳ took back His angry oath. רבי יהושע בן קרחה: 'אספו לי חסידי' is about later righteous people and martyrs, so it is no proof.

phrases.english: "Who made My covenant over a sacrifice" —
these are Chananya, Mishael and Azarya,
who gave themselves over
into the fiery furnace.
"Over a sacrifice" — these are
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets. The corrected wording adds it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues,
who gave themselves over to slaughter
for the words of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: כורתי בריתי עלי זבח – אלו חנניה, מישאל ועזריה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהושע בן קרחה's phrase-by-phrase reading of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'covenant-makers over a sacrifice' are the martyrs of later generations: חנניה, מישאל and עזריה, and רבי עקיבא and his colleagues.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא: The Desert Generation Does Come to the World-to-Come
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא holds that the דור המדבר will come to עולם הבא, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: They do come to עולם הבא, as it says: 'And the redeemed of ה׳ shall return and come to Zion with song.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא joins the argument and sides with רבי אליעזר: the דור המדבר will get to עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה pushed away רבי אליעזר's proof (step 6). רבי שמעון בן מנסיא brings a new proof for the same view. 'The redeemed of ה׳' means the people ה׳ took out of מצרים, and the פסוק says they will yet come back to ציון.

keyTerms.meaning: Those redeemed by ה׳, here the ones taken out of מצרים

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
They do come to the World-to-Come,
phrases.notes: 'They' is still the דור המדבר from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "And the redeemed of ה׳ shall return
and come to Zion with song."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 35:10

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר: בָּאִים הֵן לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יהושע בן קרחה rejected רבי אליעזר's פסוק, a new תנא brings a different פסוק for the same lenient view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The דור המדבר has a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: רבי עקיבא Was Too Harsh on the Desert Generation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that here רבי עקיבא left his usual kindness, and proves from ירמיהו that the דור המדבר must have a share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי עקיבא left his kindness behind. The פסוק says: 'I remember for you the kindness of your youth... how you went after Me in the wilderness.' If others come into עולם הבא in their merit, surely they themselves do!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן criticizes רבי עקיבא's harsh view and proves the דור המדבר does come to עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ says He remembers the loyalty of the people who followed Him into the desert, and that merit helps later generations. This is a קל וחומר: if their merit brings others into עולם הבא, it must surely bring in the people who earned it.

keyTerms.meaning: He left it, he set it aside
Kindness, going beyond what is required
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

steps.whyThisMatters: This line repeats almost word for word later in this section (step 15), about the עשרת השבטים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rabbi Akiva left his kindness behind,
as it is stated: "Go and call out in the ears of Jerusalem, saying:
I remember for you the kindness of your youth,
the love of your wedding days,
how you went after Me in the wilderness,
in a land that was not sown."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 2:2

phrases.english: Now, if others come in through their merit,
is it not all the more so for they themselves?

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁבְקַהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לַחֲסִידוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An אמורא weighs in on the תנאים argument and pushes against רבי עקיבא's position.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי עקיבא's view that the דור המדבר has no share in עולם הבא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores ה׳'s stated love for their loyalty in the desert, which merits others and so surely merits them.

steps.title: משנה: רבי עקיבא Says the Ten Tribes Will Not Return
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: רבי עקיבא learns from 'as on this day' that the עשרת השבטים are gone for good, like a day that passes.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The ten tribes will not return, as it says: 'And He cast them into another land, as on this day.' Just as a day goes and does not come back, so they go and do not come back. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: the עשרת השבטים exiled by אשור. רבי עקיבא says they will never return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads 'כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה' as a comparison: once a day is over, it never comes back. In the same way, the ten tribes went into exile and will not come back.

keyTerms.meaning: The ten tribes exiled by the king of אשור

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The ten tribes are not destined to return,
as it is stated: "And He cast them into another land
as on this day."
phrases.notes: דברים 29:27

phrases.english: Just as the day goes and does not come back,
so too they go and do not come back;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים אֵינָן עֲתִידִין לַחֲזוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the דור המדבר discussion ends, a new משנה starts on a related group: the עשרת השבטים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ten tribes will never return.

steps.title: משנה: רבי אליעזר Says Light Will Come to the Ten Tribes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads the same words 'as on this day' the opposite way: a day gets dark and then bright again, so the ten tribes will have light again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: 'As on this day.' Just as a day turns dark and then turns light, so too the ten tribes, for whom it is dark now, it will become light for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with רבי עקיבא, using the very same words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the tribes are compared to a day. רבי עקיבא focuses on a day passing forever. רבי אליעזר focuses on night always being followed by morning. So the darkness of exile will end.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: "As on this day":
just as a day gets dark and then gets light,
so too the ten tribes, for whom it is dark now,
so it is destined to become light for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view in the same משנה, reading the same words differently.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ten tribes will one day return from their darkness.
steps.whatToRemember: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא and רבי אליעזר both use 'כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה'. A day ends forever, so the tribes never return. A day always comes back after night, so the tribes will return.

steps.title: ברייתא: רבי עקיבא Says the Ten Tribes Have No Share in the World-to-Come
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא splits the פסוק: being uprooted refers to this world, and being cast into another land refers to עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: The ten tribes have no share in עולם הבא, as it says: 'And ה׳ uprooted them from their land in anger, in fury and in great rage.' 'And ה׳ uprooted them from their land' means in this world. 'And cast them into another land' means for עולם הבא. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא goes further than in the משנה. The tribes lose עולם הבא too, not only the return to the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads the two halves of the פסוק as two punishments. The first half, being uprooted, is exile in this world. The second half, being cast into 'another land', is losing עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Gemara:
The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: The ten tribes have no share in the World-to-Come,
as it is stated: "And ה׳ uprooted them from their land
in anger, in fury, and in great rage."
phrases.notes: דברים 29:27, the same פסוק as in the משנה, just its first half.

phrases.english: "And ה׳ uprooted them from their land" means in this world;
"and cast them into another land" means for the World-to-Come;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that expands רבי עקיבא's view from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ten tribes lose both their land in this world and their share in עולם הבא.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה spoke about the tribes returning to the land. This ברייתא speaks about עולם הבא. Keep the two questions apart.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: It Depends on Their Deeds
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רבי שמעון, רבי שמעון בן יהודה איש כפר עכו says that whether the tribes return depends on whether they keep sinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יהודה איש כפר עכו says in the name of רבי שמעון: If their deeds stay as they are 'this day', they do not return. If not, they return.
steps.whatsHappening: A middle opinion: the tribes' return depends on their behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads 'כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה' as describing their deeds, meaning if they act the way they act today. If they keep sinning they stay in exile, and if they do תשובה they come back.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda of the village of Akko
says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:

phrases.aramaic: אִם מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה – אֵינָן חוֹזְרִין,
phrases.english: If their deeds are as on this day, they do not return;
and if not, they return.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third reading of 'כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה', between רבי עקיבא and רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tribes' return depends on whether they do תשובה.

steps.title: רבי: The Ten Tribes Will Come to the World-to-Come
steps.stepSummary: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) says the ten tribes do come to עולם הבא, based on the great שופר in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: They come to עולם הבא, as it says: 'On that day a great שופר will be blown, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי disagrees with רבי עקיבא's ברייתא and says the ten tribes do have a share in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the פסוק, hinted at by 'וגו׳', speaks of those lost in the land of אשור coming back to bow to ה׳ in ירושלים. אשור is where the ten tribes were exiled, so the פסוק promises they will return.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for 'וגומר', and so on: the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
They come to the World-to-Come,
as it is stated: "On that day
a great shofar will be blown, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 27:13. The rest of the פסוק talks about those lost in the land of אשור coming back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: בָּאִים הֵם לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly opposes רבי עקיבא's ruling in the ברייתא, the same way רבי שמעון בן מנסיא opposed him about the דור המדבר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ten tribes have a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Again, רבי עקיבא Was Too Harsh
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן again says רבי עקיבא left his kindness. He proves from ירמיהו that ה׳ calls the tribes in the north to return and will not stay angry forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי עקיבא left his kindness behind, as it says: 'Go and call out these words toward the north and say: Return, wayward Israel, says ה׳. I will not show you an angry face, for I am kind, says ה׳. I will not hold a grudge forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: Just as with the דור המדבר, רבי יוחנן criticizes רבי עקיבא's harsh view of the ten tribes and brings a פסוק against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיהו is sent to call 'toward the north', where the ten tribes were exiled, and tell them to return. ה׳ promises not to stay angry forever, which shows the tribes are not rejected for good. That goes against רבי עקיבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: I will not hold a grudge

steps.whatToRemember: Twice in a row, רבי יוחנן says 'שבקה רבי עקיבא לחסידותיה'. About both the דור המדבר and the עשרת השבטים, he holds that רבי עקיבא's usual kindness should have led him to the lenient view.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rabbi Akiva left his kindness behind,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הָלֹךְ וְקָרָאתָ אֶת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה צָפוֹנָה
phrases.english: as it is stated: "Go and call out these words toward the north,
phrases.notes: The north is where the ten tribes were taken.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַרְתָּ שׁוּבָה מְשֻׁבָה יִשְׂרָאֵל נְאֻם ה׳
phrases.english: and say: Return, wayward Israel, says ה׳;
I will not show you an angry face,
for I am kind, says ה׳;
I will not hold a grudge forever."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 3:12

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁבְקַהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לַחֲסִידוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי's lenient view by criticizing רבי עקיבא, using the same pattern as step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי עקיבא's view that the ten tribes have no share in עולם הבא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ה׳ explicitly calls the northern tribes to return and promises not to stay angry forever.

steps.title: What was רבי עקיבא's kindness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which kindness רבי עקיבא is known for, since רבי יוחנן said he left it here.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his kindness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: where do we see רבי עקיבא's usual kindness?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 9 and 15, רבי יוחנן said רבי עקיבא 'left his kindness' when he ruled that the דור המדבר and the עשרת השבטים have no share in עולם הבא. That only makes sense if רבי עקיבא is known elsewhere for a kind ruling. The גמרא now asks where that is.

keyTerms.meaning: his kindness or piety, meaning going beyond the strict line to be generous

phrases.english: What is his kindness?
phrases.notes: 'His' means רבי עקיבא, whom רבי יוחנן said left his kindness here.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי חֲסִידוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the phrase 'רבי עקיבא left his kindness' in step 15 refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where we see the kindness that רבי עקיבא is known for.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: children of wicked Jews do not come to the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. רבן גמליאל says young children of wicked Jews have no share in עולם הבא, based on 'neither root nor branch' in מלאכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: the young children of wicked Jews do not come to עולם הבא, because the פסוק says the coming day will burn the wicked and leave them 'neither root nor branch.' 'Root' means in this world and 'branch' means in עולם הבא. These are the words of רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with a ברייתא. First comes רבן גמליאל's strict view, so that we can see how kind רבי עקיבא's answer is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל reads 'root and branch' as the wicked person's children. They lose them in this world (the root) and in עולם הבא (the branch). So young children of wicked Jews also lose their share.

keyTerms.meaning: young children, before the age of מצוות

steps.confusionAlert: This is not yet רבי עקיבא's kindness. It is the strict view of רבן גמליאל. The kindness comes in the next step, when רבי עקיבא disagrees.

phrases.english: As it is taught: the young children of the wicked of Israel
do not come to the World to Come,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי הִנֵּה הַיּוֹם בָּא בֹּעֵר כַּתַּנּוּר
phrases.english: as it says: 'For behold the day is coming, burning like an oven,'
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:19

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ כׇל זֵדִים וְכׇל עֹשֵׂה רִשְׁעָה קַשׁ
phrases.english: 'and all the arrogant and all who do wickedness will be straw,'

phrases.aramaic: וְלִהַט אֹתָם הַיּוֹם הַבָּא אָמַר ה׳ צְבָאוֹת
phrases.english: 'and the coming day will burn them up, says the Lord of hosts,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַעֲזֹב לָהֶם שֹׁרֶשׁ וְעָנָף״.
phrases.english: 'so that it will leave them neither root nor branch.'
'Root': in this world,
phrases.notes: He reads root and branch as the person's children, who will not last here or there.

phrases.english: 'nor branch': in the World to Come;
these are the words of רבן גמליאל.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: קְטַנֵּי בְּנֵי רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין בָּאִין לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer by quoting the ברייתא, starting with the opposing view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא where רבי עקיבא argues with רבן גמליאל about young children of wicked Jews.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבן גמליאל, young children of wicked Jews do not come to עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: these children do come to the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says these children do come to עולם הבא. He brings two פסוקים: 'ה׳ guards the simple ones' and the tree whose root was left in the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: they do come to עולם הבא, because the פסוק says 'ה׳ guards the simple ones.' In the cities by the sea, people call a child 'patya.' Another פסוק says: 'Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump of its roots in the ground.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is רבי עקיבא's kind view, the 'kindness' the גמרא was looking for. He rules that young children of wicked Jews do get to עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First proof: in תהלים, 'פתאים' (simple ones) means small children, as shown by the word people overseas use for a child. So ה׳ guards them. Second proof: in the dream in דניאל, even when the tree is cut down, its root is left. This means something always remains.

keyTerms.meaning: simple ones; here read as young children
the cities by the sea, overseas
the main part of its roots, the stump

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the kindness of רבי עקיבא that רבי יוחנן was pointing to. It explains why רבי יוחנן was surprised that רבי עקיבא was strict about the דור המדבר and the ten tribes.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: בָּאִים הֵם לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says: they do come to the World to Come,
as it says: 'ה׳ guards the simple ones,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 116:6

phrases.english: for this is what they call, in the cities overseas,
a small child: 'patya.'
And another פסוק says: 'Cut down the tree and destroy it,'
phrases.notes: דניאל 4:20, said about נבוכדנצר.

phrases.english: 'but leave the stump of its roots in the ground.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: בָּאִים הֵם לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבן גמליאל in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Young children of wicked Jews do come to עולם הבא.

steps.title: How does רבי עקיבא explain 'neither root nor branch'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא raises a difficulty against himself: what does the פסוק in מלאכי, which רבן גמליאל used, mean according to him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain 'it will leave them neither root nor branch'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא now has to deal with רבן גמליאל's פסוק. This line sets up his new reading of it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the children of the wicked do come to עולם הבא, then 'neither root nor branch' cannot mean the children. So the פסוק needs a different meaning.

phrases.english: But then how do I explain
'it will leave them neither root nor branch'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי עקיבא's view fits with the פסוק from step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק seems to say the wicked are left with no 'branch', meaning no children in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Root and branch mean מצוות, or soul and body
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא gives two new readings of 'root and branch': no מצוה and no leftover of a מצוה, or the soul and the body. Either way, the פסוק is not about the children.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means ה׳ will not leave them a מצוה or even part of a מצוה. Another explanation: 'root' is the soul and 'branch' is the body.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers the question from the last step. 'Root and branch' is about the wicked person himself, not his children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading one: the wicked person gets no reward left over for any מצוה, big or small. Reading two: both his soul and his body are destroyed. In both readings, his children are not included in the punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: leftovers of a מצוה, a small part of one

phrases.english: That He will not leave them
neither a מצוה nor the leftovers of a מצוה.
Another explanation: 'root': this is the soul,
'nor branch': this is the body.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא יַנִּיחַ לָהֶם לֹא מִצְוָה וְלֹא שִׁיּוּרֵי מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Root and branch' seemed to mean the wicked person's children.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Root and branch' means the wicked person's own מצוות, or his own soul and body, so the children are not included.

steps.title: Everyone agrees about children of wicked non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree that young children of wicked non-Jews do not come to עולם הבא. רבן גמליאל learns this from a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But young children of the wicked of the nations of the world do not come to עולם הבא, according to everyone. And רבן גמליאל learns it from 'and You have wiped out all memory of them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The text adds where everyone agrees: the argument is only about children of wicked Jews. Then the גמרא gives רבן גמליאל's source for the case of non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's kindness covers only children of Jews. For non-Jews, everyone agrees they do not come. The גמרא names רבן גמליאל's source for this: the פסוק in ישעיהו says their whole memory is wiped out.

keyTerms.meaning: the nations of the world, non-Jews

steps.whatToRemember: The argument is only about young children of wicked Jews: רבן גמליאל says no, רבי עקיבא says yes. For young children of wicked non-Jews, everyone agrees they do not come.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל קְטַנֵּי בְּנֵי רִשְׁעֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: But the young children of the wicked of the nations of the world,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל, אֵין בָּאִין לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: according to everyone, do not come to the World to Come.
And רבן גמליאל learns it
from 'and You have wiped out all memory of them.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 26:14

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל קְטַנֵּי בְּנֵי רִשְׁעֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the argument of steps 17 to 20 to Jewish children only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Young children of wicked non-Jews do not come to עולם הבא, according to everyone.

steps.title: From what age does a child get a share in the World to Come?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: from what point does a young child have a share in עולם הבא? רבי חייא and רבי שמעון בר רבי disagree: one says from birth, the other says from when he begins to speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: a young child, from when does he come to עולם הבא? רבי חייא and רבי שמעון בר רבי disagree. One says: from the time he is born. The other says: from the time he speaks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new but related topic: the age at which a child earns a place in עולם הבא. It lays out an argument between two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the question was whose children come. Now the question is from what age any child comes. One view says from birth. The other says only once the child can speak.

keyTerms.meaning: that he spoke, began to talk

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not tell us which of the two rabbis holds which view. It just says 'one says' and 'the other says.'

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר: קָטָן, מֵאֵימָתַי בָּא לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא?
phrases.english: It was said: a young child, from when does he come to the World to Come?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי –
phrases.english: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון בר רבי disagree:
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, so this is his son.

phrases.english: One says: from the time he is born,
and one says: from the time he begins to speak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: קָטָן, מֵאֵימָתַי בָּא לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question that follows from the topic of children in עולם הבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The age from which a child has a share in עולם הבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is an argument: either from birth, or from when the child begins to speak.

steps.title: The פסוקים behind each view
steps.stepSummary: Each side has a פסוק in תהלים. 'A people that is born' supports 'from birth.' 'It will be told of ה׳' supports 'from when he speaks.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'from the time he is born' learns it from the פסוק 'They will come and tell His righteousness to a people that is born.' The one who says 'from the time he speaks' learns it from the פסוק 'Their children will serve Him; it will be told of ה׳ to the generation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where each view comes from, with a פסוק for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'born' (נולד) shows that a child counts from birth. The word 'told' (יספר) is related to 'speak' (סיפר), so the other view links it to the time the child begins to speak.

keyTerms.meaning: it will be told, related to the word for speaking

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on when a child gets a share in עולם הבא. From birth comes from 'a people that is born.' From when he speaks comes from 'it will be told of ה׳.'

phrases.english: The one who says: from the time he is born,
learns it from what is said: 'They will come and tell His righteousness'
phrases.notes: תהלים 22:32

phrases.english: 'to a people that is born, that He has done it.'
And the one who says: from the time he begins to speak,
learns it from what is written: 'Their children will serve Him,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 22:31

phrases.english: 'it will be told of ה׳ to the generation.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for each side of the argument in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: Both views about when a child gets a share in עולם הבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 22:32 for 'from birth'; תהלים 22:31 for 'from when he speaks'

steps.title: רבינא: From the moment the child is conceived
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says a child has a share in עולם הבא from conception. He learns it from the פסוק 'Seed shall serve Him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבינא says, from the moment the child is conceived, as it is written: 'Seed shall serve Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another opinion on the question from Step 22. רבינא gives the earliest point of all: when the child is first conceived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 gave two starting points: birth and speech. רבינא goes back further, to before birth. The word זרע ('seed') in the פסוק shows that even a child still at the 'seed' stage serves ה׳ and has a share.

keyTerms.meaning: Seed, here meaning offspring at the earliest stage

phrases.english: It was stated: Ravina says,
from the moment that he is conceived,
phrases.notes: Literally 'sown.' It fits the word 'seed' in the פסוק that comes next.

phrases.english: as it is written: "Seed shall serve Him."
phrases.notes: תהלים 22:31

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: רָבִינָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the argument in Steps 22–23, giving an earlier starting point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child has a share in עולם הבא from conception.

steps.title: רבי נחמן בר יצחק: From the moment the child has a ברית מילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמן בר יצחק says a child has a share in עולם הבא from his מילה. He brings a פסוק about bearing ה׳'s fear 'from youth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמן בר יצחק says: from the moment he is circumcised, as it is written: 'I am poor and close to death from youth; I have borne Your terrors, I am numb.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives his opinion on the same question. For him the starting point is the child's מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opinion falls between 'from birth' and 'from speech.' A boy gets his מילה at eight days old. The פסוק speaks of carrying ה׳'s 'terrors' (אֵמֶיךָ) 'from youth,' and that is tied to the very early sign of belonging to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: From youth, from a very young age
Your terrors, the fear of ה׳

phrases.english: Rabbi Nachman bar Yitzchak says,
from the moment that he is circumcised,
as it is written: "I am poor and close to death
from youth; I have borne Your terrors, I am numb."
phrases.notes: תהלים 88:16. The גמרא doesn't spell out the link. It seems to read 'from youth I bore Your fear' as pointing to the mark of מילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a fourth opinion, parallel to רבינא's, on the same question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child has a share in עולם הבא from the time of his מילה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: From when the child says אמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי מאיר says a child has a share in עולם הבא from when he can answer אמן. He brings a פסוק in ישעיהו about the gates opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי מאיר: from the moment he will say 'אמן,' as it is said: 'Open the gates, so the righteous nation that keeps faithfulness may enter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more opinion, this time from a ברייתא. רבי מאיר says the starting point is when the child is able to answer אמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a later starting point, close to 'from when he speaks' in Step 22. It is more specific, though: the child must say אמן. The פסוק speaks of gates opening for a righteous nation. The next step will show how that is read as being about אמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Amen, the response that affirms a ברכה

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir:
from the moment that he will say "amen,"
as it is said: "Open the gates,
so that the righteous nation that keeps faithfulness may enter."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 26:2

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא opinion to the list of starting points.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child has a share in עולם הבא from when he answers אמן.

steps.title: Reading the פסוק as 'that says אמן'
steps.stepSummary: Using an אל תקרי reading, 'שֹׁמֵר אֱמֻנִים' (keeps faithfulness) is read as 'שֶׁאוֹמֵר אָמֵן' (says אמן). This shows how the פסוק proves רבי מאיר's point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not read it as 'keeps faithfulness,' but rather as 'that says אמן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how the פסוק from Step 26 proves that the child's share begins with saying אמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words שֹׁמֵר אֱמֻנִים sound very close to שֶׁאוֹמֵר אָמֵן. Through this reading, the gates of the פסוק open for whoever says אמן. So once a child says אמן, he has a share in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read: a way of drawing a lesson by reading the words of a פסוק in a slightly different way

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not change the actual text of the פסוק. It adds a second layer of meaning on top of the plain reading.
steps.whatToRemember: The opinions on when a child gets a share in עולם הבא are: from conception (רבינא), from birth, from מילה (רבי נחמן בר יצחק), from speaking, and from saying אמן (רבי מאיר). Each one is tied to a פסוק.

phrases.english: Do not read "that keeps faithfulness,"
but rather "that says amen."
phrases.notes: The two phrases sound almost alike in Hebrew. That closeness is what makes this reading work.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַל תִּקְרֵי ״שֹׁמֵר אֱמֻנִים״, אֶלָּא ״שֶׁאוֹמֵר אָמֵן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in Step 26 supports רבי מאיר's view.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's view that a child's share in עולם הבא begins when he says אמן
